subject: Clarify default log retention + customer purge workflow
messages:
From: Paul Lewis <paul.lewis@brightbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2026-11-27T09:18:00-05:00
Subject: Clarify default log retention + customer purge workflow

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

As part of our security review for the procurement packet, we need a concise explanation of Redwood's default retention behavior for hosted inference logs. Specifically: 

- What is retained by default for a standard hosted account (requests, prompts, generated outputs, streaming fragments, KV caches)?
- For how long are those items retained (TTL) across primary stores, cold archives, and backups?
- What is the customer-initiated purge process (steps we must follow, verification, timeline)?
- How are backups handled when a customer requests deletion — are they removed or marked/tombstoned, and what guarantees do you provide?

We also need a short playbook we can include with our security questionnaire that describes how we request deletion and how we receive proof of deletion (audit IDs, logs, timestamps, scope). I'm attaching our questionnaire and procurement timeline.

Thanks — we have an internal deadline of next Friday for submission. If it's easier to run a short call, happy to schedule.

Regards,
Paul Lewis
Head of Platform Security, BrightBank
paul.lewis@brightbank.com
Attachment: security_questionnaire_v2.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Paul Lewis <paul.lewis@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:55:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default log retention + customer purge workflow

Paul — thanks for the clear list. Putting a concise summary below and a proposed customer-facing playbook we can formalize.

Quick summary (hosted defaults):
- Raw request/response artifacts (full request text + generated tokens): default retention 60 days. These are the primary logs we surface for diagnostics.
- Prompts: treated as part of request artifact; same 60-day window unless the customer enables an opt-out or a stricter policy via account settings.
- Generated outputs: by default retained with the request artifact for 60 days. Aggregated telemetry (model-level metrics, token distributions) held for 90 days, then rolled into aggregated-only statistics (no PII) kept for analytics for up to 365 days.
- Streaming fragments / realtime KV cache: streaming fragments are not persisted beyond the session unless a customer explicitly opts to capture streaming transcripts; KV caches are ephemeral and kept in-memory / transient storage per session and not stored to disk by default.
- Backups/cold archives: routine snapshot backups exist for disaster recovery; default backup rotation is 30 days for active snapshots, with an additional cold-archive retention of 90 days before deletion unless under legal hold.

Customer-initiated purge (proposed playbook):
1) Customer opens a support request via the Redwood Support Portal or submits a signed deletion request to privacy@redwood.com. Include account ID, environment (hosted/dedicated/private), and scope (time range and/or request IDs).
2) Verification: Redwood performs requester verification (account owner confirmation + point-of-contact check). For enterprise accounts we accept SAML-asserted requests from verified admin principals.
3) Scope enumeration: engineering runs a scoped query to enumerate all primary artifacts, indexed entries, and associated backup snapshots.
4) Deletion job scheduled: primary artifacts are deleted from live stores and indexes. Backups are tombstoned and scheduled for purge as per backup rotation policy (see backup notes below).
5) Audit artifact: after deletion we return a deletion report containing a deletion-job ID, list of affected storage keys, and timestamps. This report is stored in the customer's audit log and delivered via secure link.
6) SLA: standard non-emergency purge completes within 7 business days for hosted accounts.

Exceptions: legal holds and open investigations may delay deletion. For SOC2 purposes we provide deletion reports and a summary of the runbook executed.

Next steps — I can join a call if you want to walk through the exact fields you need in the playbook. Marissa / Karthik — can one of you draft a one-page playbook (customer facing) with these bullets plus a short FAQ about backups and proof-of-deletion?

— Jonas
Lead, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Paul Lewis <paul.lewis@brightbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T08:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default log retention + customer purge workflow

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before I include it in our questionnaire: 

- SLA: you mention 7 business days for standard purges. For our risk model we need an "immediate purge" option for sensitive incidents. Can you support an emergency purge (24–48 hours) and what is the verification process for that?
- Backups: when you tombstone backups, are snapshots eventually overwritten or physically removed? We need to know whether BrightBank data could persist in cold archives beyond the purge window and if so for how long.
- Proof: the deletion report — is that cryptographically verifiable (signed ID), or is it an internal job ID and timestamps only? We may need signed attestation for audit.

Also: we want the playbook to list exact artifacts we will provide you if we request a purge (sample request IDs, time ranges, affected endpoints).

I'm attaching our procurement timeline. We can do a brief call tomorrow if that helps.

Paul
Attachment: procurement_timeline.docx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Paul Lewis <paul.lewis@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T14:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default log retention + customer purge workflow

Paul — answering the three follow-ups and giving a short playbook you can drop into your questionnaire.

1) Emergency purge SLA:
- We offer an Emergency Purge pathway for enterprise customers (SLA: best-effort 48 hours; target 24 hours when verification is automated).
- Requirements: request must come from a pre-registered org admin or via SAML-asserted API call and include scope (request IDs, time windows, and affected endpoints). For human-verified requests we require two independent admin confirmations (e.g., two separate SAML assertions or signed emails from two verified admin addresses).

2) Backups and cold archives:
- Tombstone vs physical removal: when a purge is executed we remove primary copies and mark backup snapshots that contain the artifacts as tombstoned. Tombstoned backups are scheduled for physical purge during the next backup rotation cycle. That means there is a small window where data exists in offline snapshots but is logically inaccessible and marked for deletion.
- Typical timelines: active snapshot rotation = 30 days; cold-archive purge window = up to 90 additional days. In practice, for an emergency purge we will prioritize removal from active snapshots within 48 hours and accelerate cold-archive purges to the earliest possible rotation window; for contractual commitments we can shorten the cold-archive purge window by agreement.

3) Proof and attestation:
- Deletion report contents: deletion-job ID (UUID), list of storage keys/object-IDs erased, affected time windows, and timestamps per storage tier.
- Verifiability: we can provide a signed attestation (PGP signature or similar) of the deletion report for audit purposes. The attestation is generated by the privacy team key and includes the deletion-job ID and SHA256 digests of the reported storage keys.

Customer-facing playbook (one-page drop-in):
- Submit: open support ticket with account ID + scope (time range or request IDs).
- Verify: we verify requester via SAML or signed request from 2 admins (emergency purge requires two confirmations).
- Enumerate: Redwood returns a scoped list of affected objects for confirmation.
- Execute: Redwood schedules deletion — primary stores are deleted immediately; backups are tombstoned and queued for rotation removal.
- Confirm: customer receives signed deletion report with job ID and timestamps.
- Audit: Redwood retains the deletion report for customer access and for compliance review.

Action items (internal):
- Marissa: please produce the one-page playbook PDF and the short FAQ on backups + proof-of-deletion by Tuesday EOD.
- Karthik: confirm whether we can shorten cold-archive rotation for enterprise contract language and provide exact retention numbers for on-prem/private deployments.

Paul, happy to join a 20-minute call to walk through the playbook and tailor language for your procurement docs. If you want the signed-attestation example, I can attach a template (we'll need an NDA for private key exchange). I'm attaching the internal deletion playbook draft for your review.

— Jonas Weber
Lead, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_deletion_playbook.pdf
